title: Pakicetus
summary: Pakicetus is an early relative of whales whose fossils come from river and floodplain deposits in Pakistan, dated to about 49 million years ago, in the early middle Eocene. It was found with land mammals in continental red beds, and its thickened ear bone is read as a specialization for hearing underwater sound.

uncertainty.note: NYIT gives 49 million years; Bajpai and Gingerich (PNAS) calibrate the Pakicetus-bearing interval to approximately 48 Ma. The span covers both.

where.modern_name: Chorlakki, Kohat District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan (type cranium of Pakicetus inachus; other localities in Punjab and the North-West Frontier)
where.historical_name: River floodplain beside the Tethys Sea (no human geography)

paleo.plate_model: MERDITH2021 (Merdith et al. 2021, Earth-Science Reviews 214:103477) via GPlates Web Service

importance.justification: An early whale relative that lived beside rivers, used to illustrate whale origins.

reviewer_note: Dates differ (49 vs 48 Ma); the PNAS page says Pakicetus is younger than earlier thought and that Himalayacetus (about 53.5 Ma) is older, so Pakicetus is not the earliest whale relative. Pin is Chorlakki per the PNAS page; the NYIT page gives only provinces.
